title: The Man Who Hacked A Game Show Without Cheating
sources: Wikipedia / Mental Floss / Priceonomics — In May 1984, Ohio ice cream truck driver Michael Larson recorded episodes of CBS's 'Press Your Luck' on VCRs and discovered its 18-square 'random' board actually used only five repeating light patterns.

CBS / Press Your Luck records — Knowing Squares 4 and 8 always gave cash/prizes plus an extra spin and never held a 'Whammy', Larson spun 45 consecutive times on May 19, 1984, winning $110,237 in cash and prizes, forcing CBS to pay out and reprogram the game.

lines.text: In nineteen eighty-four, an ice cream driver cracked a TV game show —
lines.caps: In 1984, | an ice cream | driver | cracked a | TV game show —

lines.text: and won a hundred ten thousand dollars without cheating once.
See, Press Your Luck flashed an eighteen-square light board.
Contestants slammed buzzers avoiding cartoon Whammies that wiped them out.
Everyone thought the lights bounced randomly.
Except Michael Larson paused home tapes frame by frame,
and noticed the computer only looped five fixed patterns.
Even better, squares four and eight had zero Whammies —
and always paid cash plus an extra spin.
Michael memorized the rhythm until his timing locked in.
On live TV, he hit spin after spin — forty-five straight turns —
while network bosses panicked and yelled cut the cameras.
Lawyers searched the rulebook, found zero rules broken,
and had to pay him every single penny.
CBS quietly reprogrammed the board the very next week.
